_comment: Metaphor-tagged archetype catalog for the staged creative front-end (the MAP stage). Each entry pairs a mechanical engine (vocabulary.ops + class_kind) with seeded-but-open metaphors. The `buildable` field here is a documentation guess only - catalog.py RECOMPUTES it at load against the live mod/contract/VOCABULARY.md and VOCABULARY_GAPS.md, so it auto-flips as the vocab roadmap ships. Ops use the exact tokens from VOCABULARY.md. `mechanic_kind` (optional) names the base-vocab SUBSYSTEM an archetype's ops need (forge / balance / discard / token / transform / exhaust / retain / rampage / tags / purge); harness_v2._pool_kind unions it with the class_kind to decide which `needs`-tagged exemplars a class is dealt. The `vocabulary.ops` list is really a VOCAB-TOKEN list (ops + statuses + conditions + scales + triggers) - catalog.live_vocab_tokens() checks each against VOCABULARY.md's backtick tokens. `description` is ONE player-facing sentence (<=150 chars, no op syntax; the picker shows it). `build_notes` is model-only construction guidance (card shapes, op syntax, touchstones); pricing/counts live in DESIGN_HEURISTICS.md archetype-notes, never here. `base_synergies` lists SHARED-POOL base-game relics/potions/colorless cards (available to every character, every run) this engine cashes in on: pieces tiered core/support with a one-line why in our own words, plus `avoid` anti-synergies, `hooks`, strengths and weaknesses. Ids are the base game's (spire-codex); only ids/names are stored, never Mega Crit's card text.

archetypes.name: Retain / hold & build
archetypes.description: Hold cards turn after turn, curate the perfect hand, then unleash it once the payoff is ready.
archetypes.build_notes: What players love here (the Watcher's Windmill Strike, Sands of Time and Establishment; Well-Laid Plans): patience that visibly pays off, and a hand that works as a curated toolkit. Give cards `retain`, bonuses for having been held (`retained_last_turn`), payoffs that read how many cards were held (`cards_retained`), and payoffs ON the held card itself (v58: a damage/Block `grow_held` that climbs each turn it stays in hand - Windmill Strike; a `held_discount` bomb that gets cheaper each held turn - Sands of Time), and enough defense to survive the build-up turns. `retain_hand` (v65, Equilibrium) keeps the whole hand this turn. (v66) `grant_keyword` gives a hand card Retain (Snap), `put_back` sets up next turn's draw (Thinking Ahead), `return_to_hand` keeps a key skill coming back (Particle Wall). (v67) `cost_delta` on "drawn" makes a held bomb cheaper each time you draw it (Kingly Kick).

pieces.why: Never discard your hand: every card is a retained card

pieces.name: Cloak Clasp
pieces.why: Block per card held at end of turn pays for holding

pieces.name: Ringing Triangle
pieces.why: Retains the whole opening hand on turn 1

pieces.name: Pael's Tears

pieces.name: Pocketwatch

pieces.name: Liquid Memories

archetypes.name: Forge / signature-blade ramp
archetypes.description: Stoke the forge all fight long, then cash it in on a signature blade whose damage climbs with every hit.
archetypes.build_notes: Forge income can come from anywhere the theme suggests: attacks that forge on hit, skills, triggers on blocking or drawing, a power, the starter relic. Don't default to a single per-turn power. Cash it in with one or two payoff attacks using `scale:"forged"`, whose printed damage grows hit by hit. For burst, prefer tools that boost ANY attack (`vigor` - v60, +N to your next Attack - Strength, temporary Strength, multi-hit) so they land naturally on the blade but still help the rest of the deck; `blade_empower` exists but is optional.

pieces.why: Triples the one blade swing that matters

pieces.name: Pen Nib
pieces.why: Every 10th attack doubles; time it onto the blade

pieces.name: Akabeko
pieces.why: Opening Vigor lands on the first blade hit

pieces.name: Prep Time
pieces.why: Vigor every turn stacks onto one heavy swing

pieces.name: Vajra
pieces.why: Strength multiplies across a multi-hit blade

strengths: Highest single-target burst in the catalog

archetypes.name: Rampage / grow-on-play
archetypes.description: One signature attack that hits harder every time you swing it, climbing from a weak jab to a finisher.
archetypes.build_notes: Use the `grow` field on a damage effect. This is ONE card feeding itself, unlike Forge ramp's class-wide counter that many cards pump. Give the grow attack cheap draw and retain support so it comes back around. Crosses well with small-deck (Ascetic) and combo plans: a thin deck redraws the grow attack almost every turn.
metaphors: each blow harder than the last

pieces.name: Nostalgia
pieces.why: The grow attack goes back on top of the draw pile every turn

pieces.name: History Course
pieces.why: Replays your last attack at turn start: a free extra grow

pieces.name: Duplicator

pieces.name: Droplet of Precognition

archetypes.name: Battle-smith / in-run upgrade
archetypes.description: Sharpen your tools mid-fight: upgrade the cards in your hand and spend the better versions right away.
archetypes.build_notes: Touchstone: the base-game Armaments, and any deck that would love Apotheosis. `upgrade_card` takes `"cards":"choose"` (the player picks one card in hand, the true Armaments feel), `"random"` (one random card in hand) or `"all"` (the whole hand). Upgrades last this combat only, so lean on retain or big, refilling hands so an upgraded card sticks around. A rare power can run a `turn_start` -> random `upgrade_card` engine. It thrives in BIGGER decks that cycle fast through many cheap cards (upgrading a whole hand turns a bloated pool efficient), pairs with draw and scry manipulation that finds the upgraded tools, and, because the class upgrades in combat, frees rest sites for healing or for Girya and Shovel.
metaphors: tools that improve as you fight

pieces.name: Jewelry Box
pieces.why: Adds Apotheosis: upgrade every card at once

pieces.name: Blessing of the Forge
pieces.why: Upgrade the whole hand for the fight

pieces.name: Razor Tooth
pieces.why: Every Attack and Skill upgrades itself as you play it

pieces.name: Stone Cracker
pieces.why: Two draw-pile cards upgrade each combat

pieces.name: Shovel
pieces.why: Or dig for relics at the rest site

Frees rest sites for healing or Girya/Shovel

archetypes.name: Ascetic / small deck
archetypes.description: Run a lean deck that cycles fast and assembles all the pieces for a win.
archetypes.build_notes: The identity is a SMALL deck. Heavy draw and cycling make a thin deck empty its draw pile every turn or two. Exhaust (`exhaust_card`: burn chosen hand cards), ethereal and purge effects let the player manipulate their deck size, and `draw_until` cycles the thin deck; example payoffs might include Grand-Finale-style finishers gated on `when:{"kind":"draw_pile_empty"}` or a few-card combo engine that wins the game if those are the only cards left. (Purge is a supporting tool the player has to EARN: gate `purge_card` behind a condition they must engineer (`draw_pile_empty`, `cards_played_this_turn_ge`), or put self-`purge` only on a costly one-shot whose play takes setup. Never a free, repeatable purge skill. A thin deck digs (v66): `retrieve_card` `pile:"draw"` tutors the card you need (Secret Weapon), `to_draw_top` replays a key card next draw, and a thin deck reshuffles often, so an `on_shuffle` power or `shuffle_hand` (Reboot) pays off.

pieces.name: Pael's Tooth
pieces.why: Removes 5, then returns them upgraded one by one

pieces.name: The Abacus

pieces.name: Stratagem

pieces.name: Unceasing Top

pieces.name: Purity
pieces.why: Exhausts up to 3 dead cards from hand

pieces.name: Scrawl
pieces.why: Draw to a full hand: in a thin deck, that's most of it

avoid.name: Mind Blast
avoid.why: Scales with a big draw pile, the opposite plan

strengths: Sees its best cards every turn
weaknesses: Status cards (Dazed, Wounds) clog it badly

archetypes.name: Venom / attrition
archetypes.description: Stack Poison on your enemies and wear them down while you stay alive.
archetypes.build_notes: Poison ignores Block, so the class wins over several turns: cheap appliers, ways to multiply or spread Poison, and enough defense to survive while it works. A power with `on_poison_damage` (v59) turns every tick into a little Block or a draw - the engine that lets the class survive while the Poison works. Cash-out (v62): `total_enemy_poison` deals damage equal to the Poison on ALL enemies (Mirage). (v67) an `on_debuff_applied` power with `status` poison pays off every Poison application.

pieces.name: Unsettling Lamp
pieces.why: Doubles the first debuff you apply each combat: a big first Poison

pieces.name: Powdered Demise
pieces.why: A second damage-over-time stacked on top

pieces.name: Sturdy Clamp
pieces.why: Keeps Block up while the poison ticks

pieces.name: Beetle Juice
pieces.why: Weakens their attacks while you wait them out

pieces.name: Dark Shackles
pieces.why: Buys a safe turn of waiting

pieces.name: Rend
pieces.why: Poison counts as a unique debuff for bonus damage

strengths: Great against one big, slow enemy

archetypes.name: Bulwark / turtle
archetypes.description: Out-defend the fight and turn your Block into an engine.

pieces.name: Sturdy Clamp
pieces.why: Up to 10 Block persists across turns

pieces.name: Parrying Shield
pieces.why: 10+ Block at end of turn deals damage

pieces.name: Vambrace
pieces.why: Doubles the first Block card each combat

pieces.name: Cloak Clasp
pieces.why: More Block from a held hand

pieces.name: Captain's Wheel

pieces.name: Prolong

archetypes.build_notes: Enemy Strength loss (v64) is Block's twin: `temp_strength_down` (Piercing Wail) blunts the hit you are about to take, `strength_down` (Malaise) every hit after. Next-turn Block (v65): `block_next_turn` banks Block for next turn (Prolong: scale block).

archetypes.name: Berserker / Strength
archetypes.description: Build Strength fast and make every attack hit harder than the last.
archetypes.build_notes: The identity is STRENGTH scaling (Demon Form, Inflame, Limit Break): gain Strength from cards, triggers and powers, and use multi-hit attacks that multiply it. Paying HP is one optional way to buy Strength, not the theme; HP-as-a-resource belongs to Blood / sacrifice.

archetypes.name: Striker / relentless offense
archetypes.description: Win by attacking: multi-hit flurries, strikes that scale, and big, splashy finishers.

pieces.name: Kusarigama

pieces.name: Pen Nib

pieces.name: Attack Potion
pieces.why: A free attack for the finishing turn

archetypes.build_notes: Cheap swings in volume, and `draw_until` (v57, Pillage) as the attack that digs through the Attacks for the one Skill or Power the turn needs. A Juggling power (`every_n` Attacks: damage to a random enemy) pays off the volume (v61). Finisher (v63): `hits_scale` attacks_played_this_turn hits once per Attack played before it. (v67) `cost_delta` on "attack_played" makes a finisher cheaper for each Attack you play this turn (Stomp).

pieces.name: Ice Cream

archetypes.build_notes: Focus drawbacks (v65): `focus_decay` (Biased Cognition: big Focus now, less every turn) and `lose_focus` (Hyperbeam) price a burst. (v67) an `on_evoke` power pays off each orb you pop.

pieces.name: Vexing Puzzlebox

archetypes.name: Commander / minions
archetypes.description: Raise a loyal minion, fight through it and keep it alive, or sacrifice it for one big burst.
archetypes.build_notes: The minion toolkit: `summon`, `summon_attack`, `buff_summon`, `heal_summon`, `shield_summon`, and `sacrifice_summon` to spend it outright for a burst.

pieces.name: Lantern
pieces.why: Energy to summon and act on turn 1

pieces.name: Prowess
pieces.why: Stats that help the fight while the minion works

Losing the minion stalls the class

archetypes.description: Invent your own buff or debuff and build the whole class around it.
metaphors: the hex of your own making

pieces.name: Rend

archetypes.name: Flow / card advantage
archetypes.description: Draw more, play more: cheap cards and card advantage chain into long, many-card turns.
archetypes.build_notes: Card advantage is the engine: draw, cheap cards and cost reduction so the player plays MANY cards a turn, with payoffs that count cards played (`cards_played_this_turn_ge`) or drawn. Where Overload spends energy on a few big cards, Flow spends it on many small ones. Draw payoffs (v62): `cards_drawn_this_turn` (Death March), rare `cards_drawn_this_combat` (Murder), `to_hand_size` refills (Expertise). (v67) `cost_delta` makes a card cheaper as the turn builds (Pinpoint: 1 less this turn for each Skill you play).

pieces.name: Brilliant Scarf
pieces.why: The 5th card each turn is free

pieces.name: Panache
pieces.why: 5 cards in a turn = AoE damage

pieces.name: Gremlin Horn
pieces.why: Kills refund energy and a card

pieces.name: Restlessness
pieces.why: Empty hand turns into draw plus energy

avoid.why: Caps you at 6 cards a turn

archetypes.name: Blood / sacrifice
archetypes.description: Spend HP as a resource, then claw it back.
metaphors: the candle burnt at both ends

pieces.name: Meat on the Bone
pieces.why: Low HP at combat end heals

pieces.name: Lizard Tail
pieces.why: A safety net for going too low

strengths: HP is a resource others can't spend

archetypes.build_notes: Self-drawbacks (v65) are prices like `lose_hp`: `lose_strength` (Friendship), `no_block_gain` (Panic Button), `dex_decay` (Wraith Form).

archetypes.name: Expose / hex
archetypes.description: Crack the enemy open with Vulnerable and Weak, then exploit it: the more debuffs pile up, the harder you hit.
archetypes.build_notes: Touchstone: the base-game Flechettes. `target_status_stacks` (v62) hits for the enemy's Vulnerable / Weak / Poison stacks (Bully). Expose (v64): `strip_block` / `strip_artifact` before the debuff; Strength Down and `doom` (an execute that never decays) count as debuffs. (v67) an `on_debuff_applied` power pays off each debuff you land (Sleight of Flesh: 3 damage to that enemy; Vicious: draw on Vulnerable).

pieces.name: Bag of Marbles
pieces.why: Free Vulnerable on everything at fight start

pieces.name: Shockwave
pieces.why: 3 Weak and 3 Vulnerable to all enemies

archetypes.name: Reaper / lifesteal
archetypes.description: Heal yourself with every hit: dealing damage and gaining life are the same action.
archetypes.build_notes: A LifeLink build: attacks heal for the unblocked damage they deal (`heal` scaled by `damage_dealt_unblocked`). Vulnerable and multi-hit get more damage through; area damage is optional, not the identity. Blight Strike (v64): `doom` scaled by `damage_dealt_unblocked` marks what the hit did not kill.

pieces.name: Omnislice
pieces.why: Damage copied to every other enemy: more unblocked hits

pieces.name: Bag of Marbles
pieces.why: Vulnerable means more unblocked damage to heal from

archetypes.name: Power engine / snowball
archetypes.description: Per-turn powers that escalate every turn until you win the long game.

pieces.name: Mummified Hand
pieces.why: Every power makes a hand card free

pieces.name: Permafrost
pieces.why: First power each combat gives Block

pieces.name: Jeweled Mask
pieces.why: A free power in the opening hand

weaknesses: Dead draws late in a fight

archetypes.build_notes: Replays (v65): a rare `echo_form` Power (first card each turn plays twice) and `replay_next` power (your next Power plays twice).

archetypes.name: Ripening / delayed payoff
archetypes.description: Plant something that does nothing now and goes off a few turns later.
archetypes.build_notes: Every ripening effect must be trackable: the player should always see how many turns are left before it goes off (shown as a buff on the player that counts down). Mix a few ripening cards with cards that keep the player alive in the meantime, so the wait feels like planning, not dead turns. A `target_intends_attack` gate (v62) times a payoff to the enemy's attack turn. `doom` (v64) is the enemy's own countdown: it dies at the end of its turn once its HP is at or below its Doom.

pieces.name: The Bomb
pieces.why: The same fantasy: 40 AoE after 3 turns

pieces.name: Stone Calendar
pieces.why: Huge AoE at the end of turn 7

archetypes.name: Balance / light & dark gauge
archetypes.description: Walk the Light or the Dark path: every card pushes the gauge, and each side has its own rewards.
archetypes.build_notes: Touchstone: Knights of the Old Republic, where you can become a light-side or a dark-side Jedi. Give BOTH poles real payoffs (`light_ge` / `dark_ge` cards worth leaning into) and `balance_step` income on each side, plus at least one `centered` card for the player who walks the middle. A run should be able to commit to one side or swing between them. Name and theme cards so their pole is obvious.

pieces.name: Duplicator
pieces.why: A double push on the gauge

pieces.name: Equilibrium
pieces.why: Retain the hand to time the swing

weaknesses: Almost no shared-pool pieces read the gauge

archetypes.name: Madness / discard-matters
archetypes.description: Churn your hand: discard is fuel, and some cards pay out when you throw them away.
archetypes.build_notes: Touchstone: the base-game Reflex and Sly cards. Discard is a resource: pair discard outlets (random or the player's choice, `scry`, discard-then-draw) with cards that are fine to play but even better when an effect discards them (an `on_discard` trigger that adds value on top of a normal play, or the `sly` keyword: discarded by an effect, the card plays itself for free). Add payoffs that react to discards, and `retrieve_card` to bring a key card back. Every card should be playable on its own; avoid cards that do nothing unless discarded. Payoffs (v62): `discards_this_turn` (Memento Mori) and `discard_pile_size` (Stack) scale to the churn. Recursion (v66): `put_back` stacks a discarded card on top of your draw pile (Headbutt), `grant_keyword` makes a hand card Sly this turn (Hand Trick), `return_next_turn` brings an attack back next turn (Bolas).

pieces.name: Gambling Chip
pieces.why: Discard and redraw at fight start: fuel pitched on turn 1

pieces.name: Beat Down
pieces.why: Plays 3 attacks from the discard pile

pieces.name: Unceasing Top
pieces.why: Discarding down to empty keeps drawing

pieces.name: Screaming Flagon
pieces.why: End turn with an empty hand = AoE damage

pieces.name: Liquid Memories
pieces.why: Pulls a card back from the discard, free

avoid.name: Runic Pyramid
avoid.why: Keeping the hand fights the discard plan

weaknesses: Random discard can pitch the wrong card

archetypes.name: Conjurer / tokens
archetypes.description: Conjure copies of your own cards into your piles: a deck that manufactures its own fuel.
archetypes.build_notes: Touchstone: Slay the Spire 1's Anger, an attack that adds a copy of itself. Conjure copies of your own cards (`add_card`, including self-copies) and give the class a reason to want the extras: triggers when cards are played or exhausted, a power that turns each copy into value, and cheap copies that fuel a combo turn. A natural fit for combo decks and for a power that helps it go off. (v67) an `on_card_generated` power pays off every card you create, Wounds included (Arsenal).

pieces.name: Vexing Puzzlebox
pieces.why: A free random card every fight

pieces.name: Crossbow
pieces.why: A free random attack every turn

pieces.name: Dolly's Mirror
pieces.why: Copies a key card for the deck

archetypes.name: Pyre / exhaust-matters
archetypes.description: Burn cards away for power: every Exhaust feeds the engine.
archetypes.build_notes: This deck wants to exhaust the cards in its hand and gets bonuses for doing so. Look for triggered effects that happen on exhaust, cards that have effects when exhausted or return something from the exhausted pool to hand or discard. `exhaust_card` (v57) is the fuel op: burn other hand cards on purpose (choose / random / up to N / all non-Attacks) so every on_exhaust payoff fires. Payoffs read the pile (v62): `exhaust_pile_size` scales damage/Block to the ashes, `exhausted_this_turn` gates an Evil Eye bonus. `exhaust_card` `pile:"draw"` (v66) burns a card in your draw pile.

pieces.name: Purity
pieces.why: Exhaust up to 3 cards from hand

pieces.name: Burning Sticks
pieces.why: The first exhausted Skill copies itself back

pieces.name: Toasty Mittens
pieces.why: Exhausts the top card every turn, +1 Strength

pieces.name: Pael's Eye
pieces.why: Exhaust the hand for an extra turn

strengths: Deck gets leaner as the fight goes
weaknesses: Runs out of fuel in long fights

archetypes.name: Strikes-matter / tag synergy
archetypes.description: A family of same-named cards that reward owning many: the more you draft, the harder the payoffs hit.
archetypes.build_notes: Touchstone: the base-game Perfected Strike. The family word doesn't have to be 'Strike': pick any word that fits the theme (Blade, Hex, Brew...) and put it in the TITLE of every card that carries the tag, so players can see which cards count.

pieces.name: Ultimate Strike
pieces.why: A Strike-named colorless card for the count

pieces.name: Seeker Strike
pieces.why: Another Strike-named card for the count

avoid.name: Claws
avoid.why: Transforms cards away from the tag

archetypes.name: Metamorph / self-rewriting cards
archetypes.description: Cards that permanently transform mid-run, so the deck rewrites itself as the run goes on.
archetypes.build_notes: Three shapes: rank-up (`transform_card` turns a weak card into a strong one once you've built up), mode-swap (two cards transform into each other as a stance or weapon toggle), and prune & graft (`graft_card` lets the player pick a weak card in hand and reforge it into a strong one).
metaphors: filing the sear, reboring the barrel
grafting a cutting onto the rootstock

pieces.name: Entropy
pieces.why: Transforms a card in hand every turn

pieces.name: Archaic Tooth
pieces.why: A starter card becomes an ancient version

archetypes.name: Overload / mana ramp
archetypes.description: Ramp your energy, then spend it on big, expensive cards and X-cost spells.
archetypes.build_notes: The mana-ramp class: energy generation and cost reduction first, then 2-3 cost cards and X-cost spells (`"cost": "X"` with `scale:"x"`) as the payoffs, with card draw to keep the big cards coming. X-cost cards are the signature: give the class a few that scale well with a big energy turn. Energy payoffs (v62): `energy_spent_this_turn` (Helix Drill) and `gain_energy` with scale `energy` (Double Energy). Whirlwind (v63): an X-cost attack with `hits_scale:"x"` hits X times. Drawbacks (v65): `no_draw` after a big draw (Battle Trance), `no_energy_gain` after an energy burst (Expect a Fight). (v67) `cost_delta` turns a big card into a bargain once paid off (Momentum Strike: after one play it costs 0 for the rest of combat).

pieces.name: Pael's Tears
pieces.why: Unspent energy pays out next turn

archetypes.name: Counterpuncher / retaliation
archetypes.description: Get hit, hit back: retaliation and Thorns turn the enemy's own attacks into your damage.

weaknesses: Useless when the enemy doesn't attack

archetypes.name: Duelist / fight-state payoffs
archetypes.description: Cards that change with the fight: execute a wounded enemy, fight harder when you're hurt, reward going without Block.
archetypes.build_notes: The `when`-gated payoffs ARE the identity: conditions the fight hands you (target below half HP, your own HP below half, no Block, a late turn) rather than a turn the player builds. Distinct from Glass tempest, which constructs its own big turn.

pieces.name: Stone Calendar
pieces.why: Turn 7 pays out: pairs with turn gates

pieces.name: Pael's Flesh
pieces.why: Energy from turn 3 onward, for late-gated payoffs

pieces.name: Panache
pieces.why: 5 cards in a turn = damage (a played-count gate)

pieces.name: The Gambit
pieces.why: Makes no-Block turns survivable, at a price

strengths: Big payoffs at the right moment

archetypes.name: Crowd-breaker / AoE
archetypes.description: Area attacks that want many enemies: the more they bring, the harder you hit them all.

pieces.name: Gremlin Horn
pieces.why: Every kill refunds energy and a card

pieces.name: Omnislice
pieces.why: Splash damage to every other enemy

archetypes.build_notes: Whirlwind / Skewer (v63): an X-cost AoE attack with `hits_scale:"x"` sweeps the room X times.

archetypes.name: Ambusher / opening burst
archetypes.description: Hit hardest at the start of a fight and aim to end it before the enemy gets going.
archetypes.build_notes: Front-loaded power: `innate` cards guarantee a strong opening hand, cheap high-impact attacks and early energy make the first turns explosive, and a few payoffs are strongest early in the fight (gate them with `when` `turn_at_most` value 2-3 rather than putting `innate` on everything). Give the class a fallback for fights that drag (card draw, a modest mid-fight plan), but its identity is fast, decisive openings. `target_intends_attack` (v62) rewards striking an enemy that is about to attack (Go for the Eyes).

pieces.name: Throwing Axe
pieces.why: The first card each combat plays twice

pieces.name: Ringing Triangle
pieces.why: Keeps the opening hand for turn 2

strengths: Ends fights before the enemy sets up

archetypes.name: Fleeting / ethereal
archetypes.description: Over-powered cards that vanish at end of turn: play them now or lose them.
archetypes.build_notes: Every card here asks a question the moment it's drawn: play it now or lose it. Ethereal cards are over-statted for their cost, but a deck can't hold many before the waste adds up, so pair them with draw, energy and cheap enablers. Crosses well with small-deck (Ascetic) and combo plans, where the same ethereal cards come around every turn. `grant_keyword` (v66) can make another hand card Ethereal for a fast exhaust.

pieces.name: Music Box
pieces.why: An Ethereal copy of your first attack each turn

pieces.name: Energy Potion
pieces.why: Play more Ethereal cards before they vanish

archetypes.name: Untouchable / exotic mitigation
archetypes.description: Negate, absorb and phase through damage instead of stacking flat Block.
archetypes.build_notes: The toolkit is Buffer, Artifact, Intangible and Blur, and the class needs an ENGINE that brings them back (a power or trigger that regrants Buffer or Blur, a ripening countdown to the next Intangible, cards that recycle a ward) rather than a pile of one-off shields. Include enough Intangible that the plan works, gated so it can't be permanent. `temp_strength_down` (v64, Piercing Wail) wards by weakening the hit instead of absorbing it.

strengths: Stronger than flat Block against bosses

archetypes.name: Glass tempest / temp-stat burst
archetypes.description: Sculpt the perfect hand over a few turns, then cash it in on one huge, stat-spiked turn.
archetypes.build_notes: Touchstone: Slay the Spire 1 Flex builds, where temporary Strength meets a hand full of attacks. The identity is SETUP: draw, retain and energy tools that let the player assemble the right hand, then temporary stat spikes (`temp_strength`, `temp_dexterity`, `temp_thorns`, `vigor` for one big attack; a rare `double_damage` turn) and cheap or multi-hit attacks that cash them in on the same turn. The player builds this moment; it isn't handed to them. Replays (v65): `replay_next` makes the next Skills / Attacks play twice (Burst); `no_draw` prices a big setup draw.
